Action Plan:
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
- 1) Acute diarrheal illness (acute gastroenteritis) – implement supportive care, dietary modification, hydration strategy, and monitoring with clear red flags and follow-up.
  - Hydration: encourage continued oral rehydration and fluid intake; consider OTC oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) to replenish electrolytes.
  - Diet: start a soft diet (crackers, toast, jam) and easily digestible foods; avoid dairy, fish, meat, and eggs while diarrhoea persists. If able to tolerate, progress to boiled vegetables and mashed foods; after 48 hours with no diarrhoea, reintroduce meat, eggs, fish gradually.
  - Probiotics: recommend yogurt with live cultures to support gut flora.
  - Medications/over-the-counter: Dioralyte suggested; no anti-diarrheal meds prescribed in this visit.
  - Activity/monitoring: maintain hydration; watch for increase in stools (6–8 per day) or dehydration; do not hesitate to contact if symptoms worsen.
  - Indications for stool testing: if diarrhoea does not resolve after one week or if blood is present in stool.
  - Education/notes: patient informed that notes are available in the app for review.
  - Follow-up: if not improved within 1 week or if worsening signs develop, contact healthcare provider; seek urgent care if dehydration signs or persistent high-frequency stools occur.
  - COVID-19 vaccine update: not applicable here.
- Additional notes: ensure patient records reflect that the app notes contain the instructions provided.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Acute diarrhea for ~3 days with abdominal pain; one episode of vomiting; 4–5 stools per day; stool described as watery/loose; no blood or mucus; mild fever possible; appetite reduced but patient able to drink.
- History of present illness: Diarrhea started 3 days ago; no recent travel or new foods; symptoms persistent despite expectation they would resolve; no external/dodgy food exposure reported.
- Past medical history: Asthma (inhaler use noted, name unclear); father had hypertension; father died of bowel cancer at age 62.
- Medications: Inhaler (name not confirmed; described as yellow); Lexapro mentioned by patient as a medication, dose/route/frequency not documented (likely not the inhaler). No other medications reported.
- Allergies: None.
- Social history: Not documented.
- Other: Patient reported mild fever; still able to drink fluids; no signs of dehydration currently.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute diarrheal illness (acute gastroenteritis)
   - Diagnosis: Acute diarrheal illness (presentation consistent with acute gastroenteritis; no red flags noted at this time).
   - Differential diagnosis: Viral gastroenteritis; non-infectious diarrhea consideration (less likely given duration and symptoms), dehydration not currently evident.
   - Investigations planned: Stool sample if diarrhoea does not resolve within 1 week or if blood is present in stool.
   - Treatments planned:
     - Hydration: continue oral fluids; use oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) as needed.
     - Diet: soft diet; avoid dairy, fish, meat, eggs during diarrhoea; gradually reintroduce foods; after 48 hours with no diarrhoea, reintroduce meat and other normally avoided foods.
     - Gut flora support: probiotic yogurt recommended.
     - Monitoring: monitor stool frequency and consistency; seek care if increasing to 6–8 stools/day or if signs of dehydration develop.
   - Referrals: None at this time.
